PBA: Marc Pingris gives thanks to PJ Simon for giving joy to people: 'Isa na ako doon'
 November 21, 2026 
 Marc Pingris said PJ Simon brought smiles to everyone around him when he was still alive. From Pingris' Instagram page 
 By Ivan Saldajeno 
 MANILA—Biñan star Marc Pingris took the moment to thank former PBA teammate PJ Simon for delivering the smiles to everyone around him.
 That included Pingris himself.
 "Tol gusto ko lang mag pasalamat sa'yo. Salamat dahil madami kang pinasaya na mga kabataan at mga manunuod sa PBA man or sa labas. Napakabait mo na tao, kaibigan, anak, at ama. Masakit man na ganito ka nawala pero nanatili ka sa puso ng bawat napasaya mo na tao. Isa na ako doon," Pingris said via Instagram just past midnight of Saturday.
 Pingris and Simon played together for Magnolia from 2005-2008 and 2009-2019, forming two-thirds of the club's "Big 3" along with James Yap.
 With the three players leading the way, the Purefoods franchise won eight titles including the coveted grand slam in 2014.
 Both Pingris and Simon eventually found their way back to professional basketball playing a few years after and became opponents in the MPBL when Simon signed with Davao Occidental.
 Simon practically retired from pro ball with finality when the Tigers opted to take a leave of absence from the regional league, but he was still playing some community league ball from time to time.
 It was during a community hoops game in Davao City on Friday night where Simon seemingly had a heart attack and fainted.
 He was still rushed to the nearby San Pedro Hospital, but he was declared dead on arrival .
 "Sakit lang. Ba't ganon paalam, tol?" Pingris asked Simon as he is still reeling from his bosom buddy's sudden passing at age 46.
 Former Magnolia imports Ricardo Ratliffe, Romeo Travis, and Marqus Blakely also bid farewell to Simon by posting reports of his passing on their IG stories.
 "Rest easy to a great human and teammate. Life is precious," Blakely said.
 The team also released a statement, saying, "Nag-iisa lang ang isang Peter June Simon. Isa si PJ sa pinakamagandang ehemplo ng isang professional basketball player. You competed with quiet confidence, carried yourself with humility, and wore #8 with a pride everyone could feel. You represented the franchise in the best way possible, and that is why you are beloved not just by Hotshots fans, but every Filipino basketball fan. We’ll always remember the eight championships and the Grand Slam. We’ll miss that signature one-hander from midrange. We’ll always think of the clutch shots and heat checks of 'The Scoring Apostle'. Most of all, we’ll miss the person we got to share those moments with. We will remember every moment, because you made each one unforgettable. To PJ’s family and loved ones, we’re holding you close in our hearts. Maraming salamat sa lahat, PJ."
